_note: Draft card content for the Physical Field Kit. Edit this file, then run `npm run build:templates` to regenerate the PDFs. The site's Physical Field Kit page reads this file too.

decks.name: Context Cards
decks.when: Module 1, once per context or setting
decks.purpose: Prompts for building a picture of the setting before you talk to anyone one-on-one. They feed the provisional codebook, glossary, and interview guide.

cards.title: People and guide
prompts: Who am I spending time with, and who is my local guide?
How does my guide know this place, and whom might they steer me away from?
Who lives or works here differently from the people I have met so far?

cards.title: Routines and relationships
prompts: What happens here at different times of the day?
Who depends on whom? Who speaks for whom?
Where do people go for help, and who do they ask first?

cards.title: Language and communication
prompts: Which languages are used here, by whom, and with whom?
Where do people switch language or register, and what seems to trigger it?
Which words, exclamations, or gestures do I not yet fully understand?

cards.title: Possible meanings and their limits
prompts: What do I think this means?
What would make me wrong?
Who could tell me, and how would I ask?

cards.title: Glossary seed
prompts: The term or phrase, in the language it was used.
Who said it, where, and to whom.
What I think it means, and what I am unsure about.
cards.footnote: Feeds the provisional codebook, glossary, and interview guide.

decks.name: Interview Cards
decks.when: Module 2, once per person or session
decks.purpose: One card per step of the one-on-one interview, from consent to correction, so nothing is skipped when the conversation gets absorbing.

cards.title: Ask for consent
prompts: Say who you are, what this is for, who will hear or see the recording, and when it will be deleted.
Ask about audio and video separately. Either can be declined.
Remind them they can skip any question or stop at any time.

cards.title: Begin with daily life
prompts: “Tell me about yesterday, from the time you woke up.”
“Tell me about the last time you had to sort out something official.”
Follow their stories. The aim is to learn how they live and to make them comfortable.

cards.title: Notice
cards.kicker: A phrase, an action, or a pause
prompts: A significant phrase (a micro comment), an action (an expression or gesture), or a pause.
Write down the exact words, what you saw, and how long the pause lasted.
Do not interpret yet. Start a Meaning Card.

cards.title: Probe heavy moments
cards.kicker: Branch: if it is hard to understand
prompts: If an emotion, expression, or gesture is heavy or hard to understand, ask what it is like.
Invite a picture, a saying, or a comparison, in their own language.
Offer a spoken idiom only after they have tried, and ask whether it fits.

cards.title: Ask what it meant to them
prompts: “Earlier you said … What did you mean by that?”
Ask in their language first. Write down their words.
Share your guess only after they have answered.

cards.title: Record correction and reaction
cards.kicker: Where you were wrong is data
prompts: If they correct or disagree with your guess, write it down as they say it.
Note how they react: a laugh, a silence, pushback.
Mark the correction status on the Meaning Card.

cards.title: Optional: observe a task
prompts: If needed, ask whether you can watch them do a task or use a service.
Notice, note, and ask in the same way as in the interview.
Capture each moment on its own Meaning Card.

decks.name: Reflection Cards
decks.when: After each session, before moving into Module 3
decks.purpose: Short prompts for the researcher, straight after a session, about surprises, assumptions, and what crossed a language boundary.

cards.title: What surprised me?
prompts: What did I not expect to hear, see, or feel?
What does that tell me about what I assumed?

cards.title: Where did I assume?
prompts: Which of my guesses came from my own background rather than from what was said?
Where did I finish a sentence in my head?

cards.title: What crossed a language boundary?
prompts: Which moments were spoken in one language and noted in another?
Who interpreted, and what might they have shaped?
Do I have all four Fidelity tags for each: source language, who interpreted, rendering, second reader?

cards.title: What needs another look?
prompts: Which Meaning Cards need a second reader, a translation review, or another question?
What new questions should go into the next round?
cards.footnote: New questions feed back into Module 1.

positionality.name: Researcher Positionality Card
prompts: Languages I speak, understand, and do not understand.
How my background differs from, or overlaps with, the people I am talking to.
How participants may see me, and what that might lead them to say or leave unsaid.
What I treat as normal that may not be.
What I may find hard to notice.
positionality.backHeading: Revisit at the end of fieldwork
positionality.backPrompt: What changed in how I see my own position?

guide.frontIntro: Cards for capturing meaning on paper, in the language it was spoken.
backPoints: Every card is 6 × 4 in (152 × 102 mm). Print at 100%, double-sided.
If a back is upside down, switch between flip on long edge and flip on short edge.
Use card stock (200 to 300 gsm) for cards that will be handled in the field.
Keep one Meaning Card per moment. Do not squeeze two moments onto one card.
Cards can be written on in any language. Do not translate exact words on the front.
